manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Stack the three bowls on the table.

Task description: Stack the three light green bowls arranged from left to right on the table, with each upper bowl nested inside the opening of the one below it.

Success criteria: After picking up and moving the bowls, all three are nested vertically, with the upper bowl bottom inside and supported by the lower bowl opening, and the stable stack placed on the table.

## Execution tips

- Choose a bowl-rim section near the robot and away from adjacent bowls, with one finger inside and one outside. Grip a short section of inner and outer wall below the rim, matching the opening to local thickness and approach clearance.
- Before closing, verify that the fingers are actually on the inside and outside of the bowl wall, rather than merely overlapping in view. After grasping, make a small test lift to check for slipping or noticeable tilt, then adjust the contact point if needed.
- Keep the bowl bottom above the rims of bowls along the route and adjust its pose where there is ample clearance, avoiding contact with neighboring bowls using the bowl bottom or gripper.
- During placement, align the carried bowl's bottom inside the receiving bowl opening and keep its opening upward. If one side contacts the rim first, lift slightly and adjust rather than continuing downward and tilting or pushing away the lower bowl.
- During nesting, watch clearance between the outer finger and lower bowl rim. Release once the upper bowl has reliable support while the fingers still have room to withdraw, then retract upward to avoid trapping fingers between the walls or lifting a placed bowl.

I have read the manual. Only the right arm is available, and the three bowls remain separated. I am adjusting the gripper pose at a raised height, then will approach the rim in small steps, grasp, and test-lift first.
The gripper is near and above the left bowl's right rim. Next I will check the opening and inside/outside wall positions, then descend gradually, with each move near contact no greater than 1 cm.

The gripper closed fully on the first attempt, and I could not confirm the bowl was grasped, so it has not been moved. I will reopen the gripper, adjust the lowering position, and check again after the pads reach below the rim.

All three bowls remain in their original positions on the table, and no grasp has been confirmed yet. The wrist view shows the rim between the fingers; I am reducing the lowering step size to check actual contact depth.

This time the gripper retains about 8 mm opening, with the bowl rim clearly between the fingers. The bowl followed the small test lift. I will raise farther to confirm stability, then move toward the middle bowl.

The bowl is off the table and remains held, but is slightly tilted. A pose adjustment was rejected at the controller limit. I will use the returned measured pose to adjust in another reachable direction and continue within this episode.

The first bowl is above the middle bowl's opening. I am centering and lowering in steps smaller than 1 cm and will release after confirming support, avoiding trapping the outer finger between the two walls.
After release, the first bowl settled inside the middle bowl; the view shows two bowls nested together. I am now handling the remaining bowl on the right.

The left rim of the right-side bowl is aligned between the fingers. I will reuse the contact height just confirmed, descend gradually, test-lift after grasping, then place it on the existing two-bowl stack.
The bowl on the right is grasped and rose with the test lift. The grasp remains secure, though the bowl is slightly tilted. I will lift it high enough first, then move it above the two-bowl stack.

The last bowl has been lifted off the table, and the grasp opening is stable. I am keeping the height as I move toward the two-bowl stack, then will lower to center it and check whether all three bowls nest stably.
The last bowl's base has entered the opening below, and the image shows it touching the stack. I will release it to settle, withdraw the gripper upward, and check whether it remains stable.
After the gripper withdrew and I observed the scene, all three bowls remained stably nested on the table. I am ending this episode now; the final success determination is for the on-site operator.
